channel.title: Kaho's Ibaraki Blog
channel.description: Stories about Ibaraki, Japan by Kaho, a local: places, food, travel tips and real life in rural Japan.

item.title: Raw egg on rice? Why Japan eats TKG for breakfast
item.description: Tamago kake gohan (TKG) is raw egg on hot rice, a normal Japanese breakfast. Why raw eggs are safe in Japan, how to eat TKG, and Ibaraki's egg story.

item.title: Nakaminato Fish Market: Ibaraki’s seafood street
item.description: A local's guide to Nakaminato Fish Market in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki: what to eat (kaisendon, sushi, monkfish), how to get there from Tokyo, and tips.

item.title: Hitachi Aki Soba: Ibaraki’s autumn noodles
item.description: Hitachi Aki Soba is Ibaraki's famous buckwheat from Hitachi-Ota. Why November is new soba season, and how to eat it: zaru, kenchin and tsuke soba.

item.title: I went to see the kochia!
item.description: The red kochia hill at Hitachi Seaside Park, Ibaraki, about 1 hour from Tokyo. When the color peaks, tips to avoid lines, and fun facts from a local.

item.title: Is Ibaraki really Japan's “least attractive” prefecture?
item.description: Ibaraki often ranks last in Japan's prefecture attractiveness survey. A local shows what people miss: blue flower hills, Fukuroda Falls, Oarai and more.

item.title: 5 things that surprise people about rural Japan
item.description: Life in rural Japan is not like Tokyo. Cars, vegetables from neighbors, quiet nights, strict garbage rules and the konbini, from a local in Ibaraki.

item.title: Overtime in Japan: what it's really like
item.description: Do Japanese people really work that much? An honest look at overtime culture in Japan, why people stay late, and what is changing, from a local worker.

item.title: Easy one-day trip to Ibaraki from Tokyo
item.description: An easy one-day trip to Ibaraki from Tokyo by train and bus: Hitachi Seaside Park, Nakaminato Fish Market and Oarai Isosaki Shrine, plus local tips.

item.title: Unwritten rules of the Japanese countryside
item.description: The unwritten rules of rural Japan nobody tells you: greetings, omiyage, the neighborhood association, returning favors and more, from a local in Ibaraki.

item.title: Hoshiimo season is here!
item.description: Hoshiimo is dried sweet potato, chewy and naturally sweet, and Ibaraki makes most of it in Japan. How it is made and where to buy it in winter.
